commands.title: Commands
commands.prefixTip: All TTS commands are prefixed with !tts.
commands.expandTip: Click any command row below to expand and see usage details.
commands.webDashboardTip: Broadcasters and viewers can also configure settings using the WildcatTTS Web Dashboard.
commands.myvoiceTip: Viewers can set their own TTS preferences using the web UI by sending !myvoice in chat.

ttsStatus.name: !tts status
ttsStatus.description: Gets the current status of the TTS application for the channel.
ttsStatus.notes: Displays engine state, mode, queue length, default voice, pitch, speed, emotion, and language boost settings.

ttsVoices.name: !tts voices
ttsVoices.description: Provides a link to the documentation section for available TTS voices.

ttsLanguageslist.name: !tts languageslist
ttsLanguageslist.description: Provides a link to the documentation section for available TTS language boost options.

ttsCommands.name:
!tts commands
(Alias: !tts help)
ttsCommands.description: Provides a link to the full list of !tts subcommands.

ttsPrefs.name:
!tts prefs
(Aliases: !tts preferences, !tts settings)
ttsPrefs.description: Sends you a short-lived link to your personal TTS settings page.
ttsPrefs.feature1: Configure your own voice, pitch, speed, emotion, and language on a per-channel basis.
ttsPrefs.feature2: Includes a red-outlined "Danger Zone" where you can add yourself to the channel's TTS and/or Music ignore lists (only a moderator can undo this).
ttsPrefs.feature3: The bot posts the link publicly in chat; it is signed for you only and expires after first access or 10 minutes. The page is pre-filled with the current channel.

myvoice.name: !myvoice
myvoice.description: Sends you a short-lived link to your personal TTS settings page (equivalent to !tts prefs).
myvoice.notes: Same as !tts prefs. The bot posts the link publicly in chat; it is signed for you only and expires after first access or 10 minutes. The page is pre-filled with the current channel.

ttsOn.name:
!tts on
(Alias: !tts enable)
ttsOn.description: Enables the TTS engine. Messages and events may be spoken based on the current mode.

ttsOff.name:
!tts off
(Alias: !tts disable)
ttsOff.description: Disables the TTS engine entirely. No messages or events will be spoken.

ttsMode.name: !tts mode [all|command|bits_points_only]
ttsMode.allDesc: (Speak all chat messages & events; this is the default mode)
ttsMode.commandDesc: (Only speak on command or for events)
ttsMode.bitsPointsOnlyDesc: (Only speak Bits cheers & Channel Point redemptions)
ttsMode.notes:
all: All chat messages (not from ignored users or commands) and enabled events will be spoken, subject to the !tts permission setting.
command: Only messages triggered by specific TTS commands (like !tts <message>) or enabled events will be spoken. Regular chat is ignored.
bits_points_only: Only Bits cheers and Channel Point redemptions are read aloud. Regular chat and commands are ignored.

ttsPermission.name: !tts permission [everyone|all|mods]
ttsPermission.description: Sets a filter on who can trigger TTS when the bot is in all mode.
ttsPermission.notes:
everyone or all: Any user's chat message can be spoken. (Default)
mods: Only messages from moderators and the broadcaster will be spoken.
This does not affect command mode.

ttsBits.name: !tts bits [on|off|min <amount>]
ttsBits.description: Configures the Bits-for-TTS feature, allowing channels to require a minimum Cheer amount to trigger TTS.
ttsBits.onDesc: on: Enables Bits-for-TTS mode. Only messages with a sufficient cheer will be read.
ttsBits.minDesc: min <amount>: Sets the minimum number of Bits required (e.g., min 100).

channelPointsTTS.name: Channel Points → TTS
channelPointsTTS.description: Create a custom Twitch Channel Point reward for viewers to redeem with a message to be read aloud.
channelPointsTTS.noteText: This feature is configured exclusively through the WildcatTTS Web Dashboard under the "Channel Points → TTS" section.
channelPointsTTS.step1: Streamer Setup: Enable the feature in the dashboard.
channelPointsTTS.step2: Reward Creation: The bot automatically creates a custom Channel Point reward on your Twitch channel.
channelPointsTTS.step3: Viewer Redemption: Viewers redeem the reward with a custom message, which gets read aloud.
channelPointsTTS.step4: Content Policy: Built-in filtering (length limits, link blocking, banned words).
channelPointsTTS.basicSettings: Basic Settings: Reward title, cost (points), prompt text, skip queue option
channelPointsTTS.advancedSettings: Advanced Settings: Global cooldown, per-stream limit, per-user limit
channelPointsTTS.contentPolicy: Content Policy: Min/max message length, block links, banned words list
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueDefault: Default Setting: This option is enabled by default for immediate TTS playback.
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueEnabled: When Enabled: Redemptions are processed immediately and do not appear in your Twitch "Reward Requests" queue.
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueDisabled: When Disabled: Redemptions appear in your Twitch dashboard for manual approval before TTS plays.
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueUseCase: Use Case: Enable for instant TTS, disable for moderation control.
channelPointsTTS.ttsModesText: Works with all TTS modes (All Messages, Commands Only, Bits/Points Only).
channelPointsTTS.requirementsText: Must grant channel:manage:redemptions and channel:read:redemptions OAuth scopes during initial dashboard setup.

ttsPause.name: !tts pause
ttsPause.description: Pauses the processing of the TTS event queue.
ttsPause.notes: New messages/events will still be added to the queue but won't be spoken until resumed.

ttsResume.name: !tts resume
ttsResume.description: Resumes processing of the TTS event queue if it was paused.

ttsClear.name: !tts clear
ttsClear.description: Clears all pending messages and events from the TTS queue.
ttsClear.notes: This command only removes messages waiting in the queue. It does not stop audio that is currently playing or actively being generated by the TTS engine.

ttsStop.name: !tts stop
ttsStop.description: Stops the currently playing or generating TTS audio.
ttsStop.note1: If TTS is currently speaking or generating audio, this command will attempt to stop it.
ttsStop.note2: Any user can stop a message if it was triggered by their own chat message.
ttsStop.note3: Moderators and the broadcaster can stop any TTS audio.
ttsStop.permission: Everyone for their own messages, Moderator for others

ttsVoice.name: !tts voice <voice_id|reset>
ttsVoice.description: Allows a user to set their preferred voice for messages they send.
ttsVoice.notes: Use reset to revert to the channel's default voice. Use !tts voices to get a link to available voice IDs.

ttsEmotion.name: !tts emotion <emotion_name|reset|auto>
ttsEmotion.description: Allows a user to set their preferred emotion for their messages.
ttsEmotion.notes: Valid emotions: neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised. Use reset for the channel default.

ttsLanguage.name:
!tts language <language|reset>
(Alias: !tts lang)
ttsLanguage.description: Sets your preferred language boost for TTS.
ttsLanguage.notes: Affects how speech is interpreted and generated. Use reset or auto to use the channel's default. See Language Boost section or use !tts languageslist for available options.

ttsPitch.name: !tts pitch <value|reset>
ttsPitch.notes: Value must be an integer between -12 and 12 (0 is normal). Use reset for the channel default.

ttsSpeed.name: !tts speed <value|reset>
ttsSpeed.notes: Value must be a number between 0.5 and 2.0 (1.0 is normal). Use reset for the channel default.

ttsIgnore.name:
!tts ignore <username>
!tts ignore add <username>
ttsIgnore.descriptionUser: For any user: Add yourself to the TTS ignore list for the channel. Your messages will not be spoken.
ttsIgnore.descriptionMod: For Moderators or Broadcaster: Add any specified Twitch user to the TTS ignore list for the channel.
ttsIgnore.permission: Everyone (to add themselves), Moderator (to add others)

ttsIgnoreDel.name:
!tts ignore del <username>
(Aliases: delete, rem, remove)
ttsIgnoreDel.description: Removes the specified Twitch user from the TTS ignore list.

ttsIgnored.name: !tts ignored
ttsIgnored.description: Lists all users currently on the TTS ignore list for the channel.

ttsEvents.name: !tts events [on|off]
ttsEvents.description: Toggles whether Twitch events (like subscriptions, cheers, raids, etc.) are announced by TTS.

ttsDefaultvoice.name: !tts defaultvoice <voice_id|reset>
ttsDefaultvoice.description: Sets the default TTS voice for the channel.
ttsDefaultvoice.notes: Use reset to revert to the system default. Use !tts voices for a link to voice IDs.

ttsDefaultemotion.name: !tts defaultemotion <emotion_name|reset>
ttsDefaultemotion.description: Sets the default TTS emotion for the channel.
ttsDefaultemotion.notes: Valid emotions: neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised. Use reset for system default (neutral).

ttsDefaultlanguage.name: !tts defaultlanguage <language|reset>
ttsDefaultlanguage.description: Sets the default TTS language boost for the channel.
ttsDefaultlanguage.notes: Use reset or auto to use the system default. See Language Boost section or use !tts languageslist for options.

ttsDefaultpitch.name: !tts defaultpitch <value|reset>
ttsDefaultpitch.description: Sets the default TTS pitch for the channel.
ttsDefaultpitch.notes: Value must be an integer between -12 and 12 (0 is normal). Use reset for system default (0).

ttsDefaultspeed.name: !tts defaultspeed <value|reset>
ttsDefaultspeed.description: Sets the default TTS speed for the channel.
ttsDefaultspeed.notes: Value must be a number between 0.5 and 2.0 (1.0 is normal). Use reset for system default (1.0).

ttsMessage.name: !tts <message>
ttsMessage.description: Immediately enqueues the provided message for TTS. This works in both all and command modes. Uses the requesting user's preferences (or channel defaults) for voice, pitch, speed, and emotion.

ttsEmote.name: !tts emote <emoteName>
ttsEmote.description: View, regenerate, or manually set cached emote descriptions used by TTS.
ttsEmote.viewDesc: View the current AI-generated description for an emote.
ttsEmote.regenerateDesc: Clear the cached description so it will be re-described by AI next time.
ttsEmote.setDesc: Manually set a custom description for an emote.
ttsEmote.notes: Emotes in chat are automatically described by AI when first encountered. These descriptions are cached permanently so they don't need to be re-generated. Use this command to view, correct, or regenerate emote descriptions.

usage.set: !tts emote set LUL = a person laughing

ttsEmote.regenerateNote: (clears cache; AI will re-describe on next use)
ttsEmote.setNote: (sets a custom description — channel emotes only)
ttsEmote.permission: Moderator (set/regenerate only for this channel's emotes)

ttsPronounce.name: !tts pronounce <word> = <how to say it>
ttsPronounce.description: Controls how TTS says a specific word or short form.

usage.test: !tts pronounce test ngl that was wild

ttsPronounce.testNote: (shows the result, but does not speak it)
ttsPronounce.addDesc: Add a word and the text that TTS speaks in its place. Your entry replaces a built-in entry with the same word.
ttsPronounce.removeDesc: Remove your entry. If a built-in entry has the same word, that built-in entry becomes active again.
ttsPronounce.offDesc: Stop a built-in entry. To start it again, use the remove sub-command.
ttsPronounce.testDesc: Show what TTS will say for some text. The bot does not speak the text.
ttsPronounce.clearDesc: The broadcaster can use !tts pronounce clear to remove all entries for the channel. Built-in entries stay active.
ttsPronounce.notes: The word is not case-sensitive, and it must match a full word. A channel can have a maximum of 100 entries. A word can have a maximum of 40 characters. A spoken form can have a maximum of 120 characters. You can also change these entries in the Web Dashboard.

ttsProfanity.name: !tts profanity <on|off|status>
ttsProfanity.description: Starts or stops the profanity filter, which replaces rude words with milder words.
ttsProfanity.statusNote: (shows the state, the language, and the number of words)
ttsProfanity.notes: The filter is off until you start it. It replaces rude words with milder words. It does not remove the message. The Banned Words list in the Web Dashboard removes a full message.

voices.title: Voices
voices.introText: The following voices are available from the MiniMax speech-2.8-turbo model via 302.ai, with automatic fallback to speech-02-turbo via Wavespeed AI. The bot uses a comprehensive hardcoded list of 472 voices with automatic language categorization across 45 languages. The voice_id is used in commands like !tts voice <voice_id>.
voices.popularText: Featured voices from the MiniMax speech-2.8-turbo model via 302.ai (with Wavespeed AI fallback). For any voice in this list, you can use the command !tts voice <voice_id> to use it.
voices.completeListTitle: Complete Voice List (from Wavespeed AI minimax/speech-02-turbo Schema — fallback provider)
voices.completeListText: This is the complete list of all 472 available voices organized by language. The voices are automatically categorized by language prefix for easy identification.
voices.expandText: Click to expand complete voice list (472 voices across 45 languages)
voices.completeListNote: Note: The bot primarily uses MiniMax speech-2.8-turbo via 302.ai, falling back to speech-02-turbo via Wavespeed AI if the primary provider is unavailable. The complete list includes all 472 voices across 45 languages, automatically categorized by language prefix. The !tts voices command in chat links to here. For the most up-to-date list, refer to the Wavespeed AI schema API or use the bot's voice validation when setting preferences.
voices.mossNote: ⚠️ Note: Some Moss audio voices may require special access permissions. If you receive a "you don't have access to this voice_id" error, try a different voice from this list.

languageBoost.title: Language Boost
languageBoost.introText: The language_boost feature helps the TTS model better understand and pronounce words from specific languages or dialects. This is particularly useful in multilingual chats or when a specific language's nuances are important for clear TTS.
languageBoost.commandText: You can set a personal language boost preference using !tts language <language_name> or moderators can set a channel default with !tts defaultlanguage <language_name>.
languageBoost.usageText: Using auto will rely on the model's automatic language detection. English is often a good default for primarily English-speaking chats. Choosing a specific language can significantly improve pronunciation for that language.

emoteDescriptions.title: Emote Descriptions
emoteDescriptions.introText: WildcatTTS uses AI (Google Gemini) to automatically describe Twitch emotes when they appear in chat messages. Instead of reading the emote code (e.g., "LUL"), TTS reads a natural description like "a person laughing." These descriptions are cached permanently to avoid repeated AI processing.
emoteDescriptions.step1: When an emote appears in a TTS message for the first time, the bot uses AI to analyze the emote image and generate a short text description.
emoteDescriptions.step2: The description is permanently cached so it only needs to be generated once.
emoteDescriptions.step3: Subsequent uses of the same emote use the cached description instantly, without any AI processing.
emoteDescriptions.managementText: Moderators can use the !tts emote command to view, regenerate, or manually set emote descriptions. See the Emote Description Management section in the commands table above for details.

webDashboard.title: Web Dashboard
webDashboard.introText: The WildcatTTS Web Dashboard provides streamers with a comprehensive interface to configure all TTS and music settings. Access it by logging in with your Twitch account.
webDashboard.settingEngineDesc: Enable/disable TTS, announce events, set TTS mode and permissions
webDashboard.settingViewerDesc: Allow or force channel default voice for all messages
webDashboard.settingUrlDesc: Read full URLs or just domain names
webDashboard.settingBitsDesc: Require minimum bits for TTS messages
webDashboard.settingChannelPointsDesc: Create and configure a custom Channel Point reward (see section above)
webDashboard.settingYoutubeDesc: Enable YouTube Live Chat TTS and set your YouTube Handle/Video ID
webDashboard.settingIgnoreDesc: Manage TTS and music ignore lists with add/remove interface
webDashboard.settingBannedWordsDesc: Block specific words or phrases so TTS skips matching messages
webDashboard.settingVoiceDesc: Set channel defaults for voice, emotion, pitch, speed, language, and text normalization
webDashboard.settingObsDesc: Get your unique secure TTS URL and detailed setup instructions
webDashboard.settingPreviewDesc: Test your current voice settings before going live
webDashboard.obsStep1Title: Step 1: Add Browser Source in OBS
webDashboard.obsStep1_1: In OBS, click the "+" under Sources
webDashboard.obsConfigUrlDesc: Paste your unique URL from the dashboard
webDashboard.obsConfigControl: ✓ Control audio via OBS (must be checked)
webDashboard.obsConfigShutdown: Uncheck "Shutdown source when not visible" for persistent audio
webDashboard.obsStep2_1: Find the audio mixer in OBS (bottom panel)
webDashboard.obsStep2_2: Click the gear (⚙️) next to "WildcatTTS TTS" → "Advanced Audio Properties"
webDashboard.obsImportantDesc: Make sure the source is unmuted in your audio mixer and volume is set appropriately.
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationIntro: Some voices may be naturally louder or quieter than others. The Voice Calibration feature allows you to set specific volume levels for individual voices, ensuring a consistent audio experience across your stream.
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationFeature1: Per-Voice Volume: Select any voice and assign a custom volume multiplier (0.1x to 10.0x). (Warning: Values over 1.0 may be loud)
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationFeature2: Auto-Apply: When a user selects a calibrated voice via !myvoice, the custom volume is automatically applied.
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationFeature3: Overrides: Calibrated volumes take precedence over the channel's default volume setting for that specific voice.
webDashboard.settingCalibrationDesc: Set specific volume overrides for individual voices to normalize audio levels

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.a1: Make sure the bot is a moderator in your channel. You can do this by typing /mod wildcatTtsbot in your Twitch chat. In many cases, the bot may need moderator permissions to read messages and respond to commands.
troubleshooting.a2: Make sure the bot is enabled in your channel. You can do this by typing !tts on in your Twitch chat. Also, check the current mode !tts mode and permissions !tts permission.
troubleshooting.q3: Bot not speaking in a specific language, or reading numbers in Chinese?
troubleshooting.a3: Make sure the language boost is set to the correct language. You can do this by typing !tts language <language_name> for yourself or !tts defaultlanguage <language_name> for the channel in your Twitch chat. You can check the current language boost using !tts defaultlanguage.
troubleshooting.q4: TTS generation taking too long or failing?
troubleshooting.a4: WildcatTTS primarily uses 302.ai (speech-2.8-turbo) with automatic fallback to Wavespeed AI (speech-02-turbo). If you experience delays, check your internet connection and try using !tts stop to cancel any stuck generation. The bot automatically retries failed requests.
troubleshooting.a5: Make sure you're using the correct voice ID from the Voices section. Voice IDs are case-sensitive and must match exactly. Try !tts voices to get a link to available voices.
troubleshooting.a6: Some voices (particularly certain Moss audio effects) may require special access permissions on Wavespeed AI. If you receive this error, try using a different voice from the available voices list. Most voices work with standard access.
troubleshooting.a7: The voice ID you're using is not available or doesn't exist. Make sure you're using the correct voice ID from the Voices section. Voice IDs are case-sensitive and must match exactly.
troubleshooting.a8: Note that "auto" emotion is no longer supported. Use neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, or surprised instead.
troubleshooting.a9: Contact the developer via the contact form at Henry's portfolio website.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Dictionary
pronunciation.introText: Chat uses many short forms that TTS speaks one letter at a time. The pronunciation dictionary changes them into words. For example, TTS speaks ngl as "not gonna lie" and glhf as "good luck have fun". WildcatTTS has a built-in list of about 70 common short forms. You can also add your own.
pronunciation.rule1: The word is not case-sensitive. An entry for lfg also matches LFG.
pronunciation.rule2: An entry must match a full word. An entry for fr does not change the word "friend".
pronunciation.rule3: The dictionary does not change text in a link.
pronunciation.rule4: The dictionary changes each word one time. TTS does not read the new text again to look for more entries.
pronunciation.customText: Moderators can add entries with the !tts pronounce command. You can also add entries in the Pronunciation Dictionary card in the Web Dashboard. Your own entries are useful for channel names, game names, or any word that TTS speaks incorrectly.
pronunciation.custom1: Your entry replaces a built-in entry that has the same word.
pronunciation.custom2: To stop a built-in entry, use !tts pronounce off <word>. To start it again, use !tts pronounce remove <word>.
pronunciation.custom3: A channel can have a maximum of 100 entries.
pronunciation.switchText: The dictionary is on for all channels. To stop it, set the "Expand Chat Acronyms" control to off in the Web Dashboard. TTS then speaks each short form one letter at a time.
pronunciation.lolTip: TTS already speaks lol as "el oh el". This is the usual result, and there is no dictionary entry for it.

profanityFilter.title: Profanity Filter
profanityFilter.introText: The profanity filter replaces rude words with milder words before TTS speaks them. For example, TTS speaks "what the fuck" as "what the freak". The filter is off until a moderator starts it.
profanityFilter.startText: Use !tts profanity on in chat, or set the "Profanity Filter" control to on in the Web Dashboard. Use !tts profanity status to see the state, the language, and the number of words in the list.
profanityFilter.behavior1: The filter replaces a rude word with a milder word. It does not remove the message, and it does not make a bleep sound.
profanityFilter.behavior2: The filter replaces a slur with the word "slur". This replacement keeps the meaning of the slur out of the audio.
profanityFilter.behavior3: The filter also applies to short forms from the pronunciation dictionary. When the filter is on, TTS speaks lfg as "let's freaking go".
profanityFilter.behavior4: A word must match fully. The filter does not change the word "class".
profanityFilter.languageText: The filter has word lists for all 40 languages that Language Boost supports. The filter uses the list for your channel language. If a viewer selects a different language for their own messages, the filter uses both lists. The filter always includes the English list, because the pronunciation dictionary is in English.
profanityFilter.languageAutoText: If your Language Boost is "Automatic", the filter uses the English list. The bot cannot identify the language of each message.
profanityFilter.languageCoverageText: The English list is the largest. The lists for other languages are smaller. Slurs are in the English list only.
profanityFilter.bannedWordsTip: The profanity filter is not the same as the Banned Words list. Banned Words removes the full message. The profanity filter speaks the message, but with milder words.

bannedWords.title: Banned Words
bannedWords.introText: The Banned Words feature stops WildcatTTS from speaking unwanted messages. If a chat message contains a banned word or phrase, TTS skips the message completely. The bot does not generate audio for skipped messages.
bannedWords.rule1: Matching is not case-sensitive. If you ban "badword", TTS also catches "BadWord" and "BADWORD".
bannedWords.rule2: TTS matches parts of words. If you ban "spam", TTS also skips messages that contain "spammer" or "spammy".
bannedWords.rule3: You can ban multi-word phrases. For example, you can ban phrases such as "follow my link" or "free followers".
bannedWords.rule4: TTS ignores the username in replies. If a reply mentions a user with a banned word in their name, TTS does not skip the message.
bannedWords.eventsIntro: The bot handles events and chat messages differently when a message contains a banned word:
bannedWords.eventChat: Chat Messages: TTS skips the full message. No voice audio plays.
bannedWords.eventResub: Resubscriptions: The bot announces the resubscription, but omits the attached viewer message.
bannedWords.eventStreak: Watch Streaks: The bot announces the streak count, but omits the attached viewer message.
bannedWords.eventRedemption: Channel Point Redemptions: The bot announces the reward redemption, but omits the custom text input.
bannedWords.eventRewardPolicy: Custom Reward Policy: If a Channel Point reward has a content policy, the bot rejects redemptions that contain banned words.
bannedWords.manageIntro: You can configure banned words in the Web Dashboard. Changes take effect immediately.
bannedWords.step1: Log in to the Web Dashboard at tts.wildcat.chat with your Twitch account.
bannedWords.step2: Scroll to the Banned Words / Phrases card below the Ignore List section.
bannedWords.step3: Type a word or phrase into the input field.
bannedWords.step4: Click Add, or press Enter on your keyboard.
bannedWords.step5: If you want to remove an entry, click Remove next to the word in the list.
bannedWords.comparisonTip: Banned Words skips the full message. The Profanity Filter speaks the message with milder words. If a message contains words on both lists, TTS skips the message.
